items.context: The dashboard would be a new page within the swarm-manager UI, which already has an overview API endpoint and tabbed navigation. No acceptance_allow patterns were set on the spec. The swarm-manager is the natural home since the overview data (backlog stats, initiatives, dependency graph) is its domain.

options.label: scenarios/swarm-manager/ui/src/**
options.rationale: Most natural fit — overview API already exists, UI already has tabbed layout, all backlog/initiative/execution data is here. Only UI files change.

options.label: scenarios/swarm-manager/**
options.rationale: Broader scope — allows for API changes too if needed (e.g., adding fields to overview response).

options.label: Targeted subdirectories only
options.rationale: Restrict to specific subdirectories for tighter change boundaries.

items.notes: Pre-selected A because the plan calls for no new backend endpoints — all data comes from existing APIs.

items.context: The overview API returns: summary stats (total items, by-status, by-kind, active initiatives), initiative rollups, and dependency graph (edges, blocked, unblocked). Execution data is available from separate endpoints. The question is which widgets to include in v1 vs defer.

options.label: Minimal: summary stat cards + blocked items only
options.rationale: Fastest to ship. Answers 'what needs attention?' without complexity. Can expand later.

options.label: Standard: stats + blocked items + initiative progress + recent activity
options.rationale: Covers the main use cases (status, blockers, progress, activity). Moderate effort, good value.

options.label: Full: Standard + dependency graph visualization + scenario health
options.rationale: Most comprehensive. Dependency graph viz adds significant complexity (layout algorithms, interactive nodes). May be premature for v1.

items.notes: Pre-selected B as the best value/effort ratio. Dependency graph visualization (option C) is interesting but complex — better as a follow-up.

items.context: The swarm-manager UI currently has 5 tabs: Backlog, Scenarios, Execution, Prompts, Settings. Adding Dashboard as a 6th tab (first position) changes the navigation layout. On mobile with bottom-nav, 6 tabs may be tight.

options.label: Add Dashboard as 6th tab (first position), icon-only on mobile
options.rationale: Clean separation. Dashboard gets its own tab. Use icons on mobile to save space.

options.label: Replace the index redirect — Dashboard is the Backlog page's default sub-view
options.rationale: No new tab needed. Dashboard becomes a 'summary' view within Backlog. But conflates two concepts.

options.label: Add Dashboard tab, merge Prompts into Settings to keep 5 tabs
options.rationale: Keeps tab count at 5. But Prompts may be too different from Settings to merge cleanly.

items.notes: No pre-selection — this is a UX decision that benefits from user input. Option A is the most straightforward but option C is worth considering if tab crowding is a concern.

items.context: The dashboard shows point-in-time data. Operators may leave it open as a monitoring view. Options range from manual refresh to polling to server-sent events.

options.label: Fetch on mount only (manual refresh via browser)
options.rationale: Simplest. No polling overhead. Users can refresh the page. Good for v1.

options.label: Auto-poll every 60 seconds with manual refresh button
options.rationale: Good UX for a monitoring view. Moderate complexity. Configurable interval via Settings.

options.label: Server-Sent Events for real-time updates
options.rationale: Best UX but requires new backend infrastructure (SSE endpoint). Over-engineered for v1.

items.notes: Pre-selected B — polling with a refresh button is the standard pattern for dashboard views. SSE is a nice-to-have for later.

items.topic: Acceptance file paths — what files should this work modify?
items.context: Since acceptance_allow patterns should target swarm-manager, we need to define which file paths are expected to change. This is a UI-only change with no new backend endpoints.

options.label: Targeted: scenarios/swarm-manager/ui/src/**
options.rationale: Only UI files change. New page, new components, route update, nav update.

options.label: Broader: scenarios/swarm-manager/**
options.rationale: Allows for API changes too if needed (e.g., adding fields to overview response).

items.notes: Pre-selected A since the plan calls for no new backend endpoints — all data comes from existing APIs.

items.text: The swarm-manager already has a GET /api/v1/overview endpoint (api/internal/overview/) that returns backlog items, initiatives with rollup, dependency graph (edges/blocked/unblocked), and summary stats (total items, items by status/kind, active initiatives). This data source is ready to consume — no backend work needed for the core dashboard widgets.

Multiple other Vrooli scenarios have dashboard implementations that can serve as reference patterns: browser-automation-studio (widget-based with tabs), lifestyle-dashboard (domain cards + timeline), test-genie (stats + guided flows), knowledge-observatory, vrooli-autoheal, and vrooli-onboarding. The browser-automation-studio DashboardView is the most feature-rich reference.
